400.description:
## Bad Request

### Invalid parameters - Type: "errors/invalid_parameters"
One or more request parameters are invalid or missing.

### Missing parameters - Type: "errors/missing_parameters"
One or more request parameters are missing.

### Invalid parameters - Type: "errors/invalid_request"
One or a combination of request parameters are invalid.

### Malformed request - Type: "errors/malformed_request"
The given request has been rejected by the provider.

### Content too large - Type: "errors/content_too_large"
The request payload or filter query is too large and has been rejected by the provider.

### Too many characters - Type: "errors/too_many_characters"
The provided content exceeds the character limit.

### Unescaped characters - Type: "errors/unescaped_characters"
The request path contains unescaped characters.

### Limit too high - Type: "errors/limit_too_high"
Provider cannot accept such high pagination limit. See API reference for details.

### Invalid action - Type: "errors/invalid_action"
This action is invalid.

### Invalid label - Type: "errors/invalid_label"
This label is invalid.

401.description:
## Unauthorized

### Missing credentials - Type: "errors/missing_credentials"
Some credentials are necessary to perform the request.

### Multiple sessions - Type: "errors/multiple_sessions"
LinkedIn limits the use of multiple sessions on certain Recruiter accounts. This error restricts access to this route only, but causing a popup to appear in the user's browser, prompting them to choose a session, which can disconnect the current account. To avoid this error, use the cookie connection method.

### Wrong account - Type: "errors/wrong_account"
The provided credentials do not match the correct account.

### Invalid credentials - Type: "errors/invalid_credentials"
The provided credentials are invalid.

### Invalid proxy credentials - Type: "errors/invalid_proxy_credentials"
The provided proxy credentials are invalid.

### Invalid IMAP configuration - Type: "errors/invalid_imap_configuration"
The provided IMAP configuration is invalid.

### Invalid SMTP configuration - Type: "errors/invalid_smtp_configuration"
The provided SMTP configuration is invalid.

### Invalid checkpoint solution - Type: "errors/invalid_checkpoint_solution"
The checkpoint resolution did not pass successfully. Please retry.

### Checkpoint error - Type: "errors/checkpoint_error"
The checkpoint does not appear to be resolvable. Please try again and contact support if the problem persists.

### Expired credentials - Type: "errors/expired_credentials"
Invalid credentials. Please check your username and password and try again.

### Expired link - Type: "errors/expired_link"
This link has expired. Please return to the application and generate a new one.

### Insufficient privileges - Type: "errors/insufficient_privileges"
This resource seems to be out of your scopes.

### Disconnected account - Type: "errors/disconnected_account"
The account appears to be disconnected from the provider service.

### Disconnected feature - Type: "errors/disconnected_feature"
The service you're trying to reach appears to be disconnected.

500.description:
## Internal Server Error

### Unexpected error - Type: "errors/unexpected_error"
Something went wrong. {{moreDetails}}

### Provider error - Type: "errors/provider_error"
The provider is experiencing operational problems. Please try again later.

### Authentication intent error - Type: "errors/authentication_intent_error"
The current authentication intent was killed after failure. Please start the process again from the beginning.

503.description:
## Service Unavailable

### No client session - Type: "errors/no_client_session"
No client session is currently running.

### No channel - Type: "errors/no_channel"
No channel to client session.

### Handler missing - Type: "errors/no_handler"
Handler missing for that request.

### Network down - Type: "errors/network_down"
Network is down on server side. Please wait a moment and retry.

### Service unavailable - Type: "errors/service_unavailable"
Please try again later.

504.description:
## Gateway Timeout

### Request timed out - Type: "errors/request_timeout"
Request Timeout. Please try again, and if the issue persists, contact support.

post.description: Link to Uniple an account of the given type and provider.

requestBody.description: The parameters required to perform the authentication depend on the type of account you are trying to connect.

anyOf.title: Linkedin
anyOf.description: There is two different ways to authenticate a Linkedin account. Each way can benefit from some proxy options.

anyOf.title: Basic authentication
anyOf.description: Authenticate using your username and password

country.description: An ISO 3166-1 A-2 country code to be set as proxy's location.

ip.description: An IPv4 address to infer proxy's location.

disabled_features.description: An array of features that should be disabled for this account.

sync_limit.description: Set a sync limit either for chats, messages or both. Chats limit will apply to each inbox, whereas messages limit will apply to each chat. No value will not apply any limit (default behaviour). Providers partial support.

chats.description: Either a UTC Datetime to start sync from, or a quantity of data.

anyOf.description: An ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ). ⚠️ All links expire upon daily restart, regardless of their stated expiration date. A new link must be generated each time a user clicks on your app to connect.
The quantity of data that should be synced from data history. 0 will not sync history.

messages.description: Either a UTC Datetime to start sync from, or a quantity of data.

anyOf.description: An ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ). ⚠️ All links expire upon daily restart, regardless of their stated expiration date. A new link must be generated each time a user clicks on your app to connect.
The quantity of data that should be synced from data history. 0 will not sync history.

user_agent.description: If encountering disconnection issues, enter the exact user agent of the browser on which the account has been connected. You can easily retrieve it in the browser's console with this command : "console.log(navigator.userAgent)"

recruiter_contract_id.description: The contract that should be used with Linkedin Recruiter.

username.description: Should be either an email address or a phone number.

post.description: Reconnect an account previously linked to Unipile that has been disconnected.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The id of the account to reconnect.

requestBody.description: The parameters required to perform the authentication depend on the type of account you are trying to connect.

anyOf.title: Linkedin
anyOf.description: There is two different ways to authenticate a Linkedin account. Each way can benefit from some proxy options.

anyOf.title: Basic authentication
anyOf.description: Authenticate using your username and password

country.description: An ISO 3166-1 A-2 country code to be set as proxy's location.

ip.description: An IPv4 address to infer proxy's location.

disabled_features.description: An array of features that should be disabled for this account.

sync_limit.description: Set a sync limit either for chats, messages or both. Chats limit will apply to each inbox, whereas messages limit will apply to each chat. No value will not apply any limit (default behaviour). Providers partial support.

chats.description: Either a UTC Datetime to start sync from, or a quantity of data.

anyOf.description: An ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ). ⚠️ All links expire upon daily restart, regardless of their stated expiration date. A new link must be generated each time a user clicks on your app to connect.
The quantity of data that should be synced from data history. 0 will not sync history.

messages.description: Either a UTC Datetime to start sync from, or a quantity of data.

anyOf.description: An ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ). ⚠️ All links expire upon daily restart, regardless of their stated expiration date. A new link must be generated each time a user clicks on your app to connect.
The quantity of data that should be synced from data history. 0 will not sync history.

user_agent.description: If encountering disconnection issues, enter the exact user agent of the browser on which the account has been connected. You can easily retrieve it in the browser's console with this command : "console.log(navigator.userAgent)"

recruiter_contract_id.description: The contract that should be used with Linkedin Recruiter.

username.description: Should be either an email address or a phone number.

anyOf.description: Authenticate using cookies

The quantity of data that should be synced from data history. 0 will not sync history.

access_token.description: Linkedin access token, which is to be found under the key "li_at".

premium_token.description: Linkedin Recruiter/Sales Navigator authentication cookie, which is to be found under the key "li_a". It should be used if you need to be logged to an existing session. It not provided, a new session will be started.

anyOf.title: Whatsapp
anyOf.description: Connect a Whatsapp account.By default, this use the QR code authentication.

country.description: An ISO 3166-1 A-2 country code to be set as proxy's location.

ip.description: An IPv4 address to infer proxy's location.

disabled_features.description: An array of features that should be disabled for this account.

pairing_phone_number.description: The phone number to login with phone number. Format: E.164 digits only (country code + number), e.g. 33600000000. Non-digits are ignored. A code to be entered in the Whatsapp app will be returned as a checkpoint. If this field is left empty, a QR code to be scanned will be returned as a checkpoint.

get.description: This route can be used both to initiate a sync process (from scratch or within a specific time span) and to monitor its status via regular polling. Supported providers: LinkedIn and Telegram. Instagram and WhatsApp are not supported by this route.

parameters.name: chunk_size
parameters.description: The number of chats to be synchronized in a single chunk. Supported for LinkedIn and Telegram.

parameters.name: partial
parameters.description: LinkedIn only. Whether the account should be partially resynchronized (keeping already synced data) or fully resynchronized.

parameters.name: linkedin_product
parameters.description: LinkedIn only. The LinkedIn messaging feature to synchronize. Leave blank to process all connected features.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The end of the time span (lowest Epoch time in ms). Supported for LinkedIn and Telegram.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The start of the time span (highest Epoch time in ms). Supported for LinkedIn and Telegram.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: The id of the account to resynchronize.

status.description: The status of the synchronization. You can setup a regular polling on the same route to get updates on its status. A new request after a SYNC_DONE, CHUNK_DONE or SYNC_ERROR response will start a fresh sync.

post.description: Allows you to provide a code which will solve a checkpoint encountered during a native authentication. A checkpoint is a security step added by a provider which needs to be solved to complete the authentication. Checkpoints that require a code are 2FA (two-factor authentication) and OTP (one-time password). Depending on the way you have configured the account you are trying to authenticate, you can get your code from various ways such as a mail, a SMS or from a two-factor authentication app.

schema.title: Checkpoint code is required to pass authentication (2FA, OTP...)

code.description: The code to solve the checkpoint. If the code is a phone number, it should be preceded by the international dialling code in brackets (e.g. (+33)0612345678 for France). If you need to switch to a different type of checkpoint, enter TRY_ANOTHER_WAY here (e.g. from In app validation to 2FA).

201.description: Created. The code is valid and the authentication is completed.

get.description: Returns a list of emails.

parameters.name: message_id
parameters.description: A filter to target items by message_id.

parameters.name: thread_id
parameters.description: A filter to target items by thread identifier.

parameters.name: meta_only
parameters.description: Speed up the response by only returning the email metadata, excluding the body and attachments metadata.

parameters.description: Include the email headers in the response. `meta_only` must be false.

schema.description: A filter to target items created before the datetime (exclusive). Must be an ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).
A filter to target items created after the datetime (exclusive). Must be an ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).
A limit for the number of items returned in the response. The value can be set between 1 and 250.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search applied to subject and body at the same time. Microsoft: requests combining search with from, to, any_email, before, after, thread_id, message_id or exclude_folders are rejected with invalid_request. IMAP: can be slow, only available within one folder, specified with folder or role, before and after are evaluated at day granularity, support depends on the IMAP server. IMAP requests combining search with any_email, exclude_folders, thread_id, multiple from values or multiple to values are rejected with invalid_request.

parameters.name: any_email

parameters.name: to

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: A filter to target items related to a certain sender.

parameters.name: exclude_folders
parameters.description: A filter to exclude items from a comma-separated list of folder provider_id ( ignored if folder parameter is used ).

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: A filter to target items related to a certain folder provider_id.

text.description:
The message that will start the new conversation.
With LinkedIn recruiter, a range of HTML tags can be used directly in the body of the message to enhance the presentation. The supported tags are <strong> for bold text, <em> for italic text, <a href="www.my-link.com"> for external links, <ul> for unordered lists, <ol> for ordered lists and <li> for list items. Tags can be nested into each other if necessary.

video_message.description: (Linkedin) A file to send as video message. WhatsApp: use attachments field.

attendees_ids.description:

For `instagram`, please use the 'provider_messaging_id'.
For LinkedIn users, use a `provider_id` starting with: ACo for classic, ACw for Sales Navigator, AE for Recruiter.
For LinkedIn company messaging, please use the 'messaging_id'.

patch.summary: Perform an action on a given chat
patch.description: Perform an action like changing the read status, muting the chat, retrieving a group invite link, etc.

parameters.name: chat_id
parameters.description: The id of the chat to be patched

action.description:
The action to perform on the chat:
       - `setReadStatus`: (WhatsApp & LinkedIn only) Set the read status of the chat.
       - `setMuteStatus`: (WhatsApp & LinkedIn only) Set the mute status of the chat.
       - `setArchiveStatus`: (WhatsApp only) Set the archive status of the chat.
       - `setPinnedStatus`: (WhatsApp only) Set the pinned status of the chat.
       - `addParticipant`: (WhatsApp & Telegram only) Add a participant to the group chat.
         The account owner must have the Add other members permission in the group.
         Provide the provider ID as value, for example 334455667788@s.whatsapp.net for WhatsApp,
         or a Telegram user ID, username, or phone number for Telegram.
       - `removeParticipant`: (WhatsApp & Telegram only) Remove a participant from the group chat.
         Provide the provider ID as value, for example 334455667788@s.whatsapp.net for WhatsApp,
         or a Telegram user ID, username, or phone number for Telegram.
       - `setLabel`: (WhatsApp only) Add a label to the chat.
         If the label does not exist, it will be created and then assigned.
       - `getInviteLink`: (WhatsApp & Telegram only) Generate or retrieve the full group invite link.
         The account owner must have the required invite permissions in the group.

value.description: Required for every action except `getInviteLink`. Use a boolean for status actions and a string for participant or label actions.

invite_link.description: The full group invite link. Only returned for the `getInviteLink` action.

get.description: Returns a list of calendar events related to the given calendar.

parameters.name: expand_recurring
parameters.description: Filter events by type (single or occurence).

parameters.name: event_type
parameters.description: Filter events by event type. This parameter accepts a comma-delimited list of event type.

parameters.name: attendees
parameters.description: Filter events with attendees contained in this list. This parameter accepts a comma-delimited list of email addresses.

parameters.name: updated_after
parameters.description: Filter events updated after this date. Preferred format: RFC3339 datetime (`2026-02-27T17:07:49Z`).

parameters.name: updated_before
parameters.description: Filter events updated before this date. Preferred format: RFC3339 datetime (`2026-02-27T17:07:49Z`).

parameters.name: busy
parameters.description: Filter for events with the status `busy`

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Filter events ending before this date. Preferred format: RFC3339 datetime (`2026-02-27T17:07:49Z`).

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Filter events starting after this date. Preferred format: RFC3339 datetime (`2026-02-27T17:07:49Z`).

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Filter for events matching the specified location.

parameters.name: ical_uid
parameters.description: Filter for events matching the specified iCal UID.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Filter for events matching the specified description.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Filter for events matching the specified title.

parameters.name: is_cancelled
parameters.description: Indicates if you want to retrieve the cancelled events.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: An offset used for pagination, if supported by the provider, else use `cursor`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The limit of items to be returned.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: The id of the account to use.

parameters.name: calendar_id
parameters.description: The id of the calendar related to events

id.description: The ID of the calendar event.

ical_uid.description: The iCalendar UID of the event, as defined in RFC5545.

master_event_id.description: If event instance, the ID of the master event.

calendar_id.description: The ID of the calendar the event belongs to.

created_at.description: The date the event was created. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

updated_at.description: The date the event was last updated. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

is_attendees_list_hidden.description: Is the attendees list hidden for attendees.

items.description: An attendee of a calendar event.

comment.description: The response comment of the attendee.

is_organizer.description: Is the attendee the organizer of the event.

is_optional.description: Is the attendee optional (based on type).

is_resource.description: Is the attendee a resource (based on type).

response_status.description: The response status of the attendee. `yes` if the invitation is accepted. `no` if the invitation is declined. `maybe` if the attendee is not sure. `noreply` if the invitation is pending.

start.description: The start date and time of the event.

date_time.description: The date and time. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

time_zone.description: The time zone of the date time.

date.description: The date. Uses ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD).

end.description: The end date and time of the event.

date_time.description: The date and time. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

time_zone.description: The time zone of the date time.

date.description: The date. Uses ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD).

recurrence.description: List of RRULE, EXRULE, RDATE and EXDATE lines for a recurring event, as specified in RFC5545.

url.description: The conference URL. If not provided, it will automatically create a new conference (only teams and google_meet available)

transparency.description: The transparency of the event. `opaque` does block time on the calendar and is equivalent to setting Show me as to Busy in the Calendar UI. `transparent` does not block time on the calendar and is equivalent to setting Show me as to Available in the Calendar UI.

guests_can_modify.description:
If true, allow guests to modify the event.
`Outlook Calendar`: Not supported, this parameter will always be false.

next_cursor.description: Cursor to get the next page of results if supported. Else use `offset`.

id.description: The ID of the calendar event.

ical_uid.description: The iCalendar UID of the event, as defined in RFC5545.

master_event_id.description: If event instance, the ID of the master event.

calendar_id.description: The ID of the calendar the event belongs to.

created_at.description: The date the event was created. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

updated_at.description: The date the event was last updated. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

is_attendees_list_hidden.description: Is the attendees list hidden for attendees.

items.description: An attendee of a calendar event.

comment.description: The response comment of the attendee.

is_organizer.description: Is the attendee the organizer of the event.

is_optional.description: Is the attendee optional (based on type).

is_resource.description: Is the attendee a resource (based on type).

response_status.description: The response status of the attendee. `yes` if the invitation is accepted. `no` if the invitation is declined. `maybe` if the attendee is not sure. `noreply` if the invitation is pending.

start.description: The start date and time of the event.

date_time.description: The date and time. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

time_zone.description: The time zone of the date time.

date.description: The date. Uses ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD).

end.description: The end date and time of the event.

date_time.description: The date and time. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

time_zone.description: The time zone of the date time.

get.description: Retrieve the profile of a user. Ensure careful implementation of this action and consult provider limits and restrictions: https://developer.unipile.com/docs/provider-limits-and-restrictions

schema.description:
A list of profile sections to retrieve detailed information on a LinkedIn profile.
LinkedIn may throttle heavy use of full data section requests, so pick only the sections you truly need.
Select *_preview to fetch all sections with preview data (first entries as displayed in the LinkedIn profile UI), or * to fetch all sections with full data (not recommended if you’re chaining a lot of profile calls in a short period).
You can also combine selectors, for example, `["*_preview", "experience", "skills"]` to get all sections in preview plus experience and skills in full.
In the response, you may receive empty sections if LinkedIn is throttling your requests. In such case, the `throttled_sections` field lists the concerned sections. To prevent this, you should add random delay between your calls, and/or not request as many sections as you use to.

post.description: Publish a post.

account_id.description: The id of the account to perform the request from.

text.description:
`Linkedin`: You can add a mention by inserting the index of the corresponding entry from the mentions array between two double braces. Example: Hey {{0}}, check this out !
`Instagram`: To mention a user, use the @ symbol followed by their username. On a story, each mention is drawn on the media as a tappable `@username` sticker and the user is notified; the surrounding text is not displayed. A username that matches no account is left as plain text. Up to 10 mentions per story.

attachments.description: On `linkedin`, image file resolution is limited to 6012px x 6012px max.

repost.description: The id of an existing LinkedIn post to publish as repost. For a simple repost without commentary, `text` should be an empty string.

include_job_posting.description: `Linkedin only` The ID of a job posting that should be displayed within a preview card.

name.description: The name of the user as it will be displayed in your message.

profile_id.description: The provider ID of the user, which begins with ACo/ADo for individuals and is a series of digits for companies.

external_link.description: `Linkedin only` An external link that should be displayed within a preview card. The URL must also be included in the post textual content. Otherwise, it will be automatically added at the end.

as_organization.description: `Linkedin only` Provide the ID of an organization over which you have control to perform the action on its behalf.

location.description: `Instagram only`: The location to tag in the post. The best match for the query is used, and a query matching no place leaves the post untagged. On a story, the location is also drawn on the media as a tappable sticker.

post_type.description: `Instagram only`: Publish as a regular feed post or as a story. Defaults to `feed` when omitted or empty.

get.summary: List all comments from a post
get.description: Returns a list of either comments on a given post or replies on a given comment.

schema.description: A limit for the number of items returned in the response. The value can be set between 1 and 100.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: The sort method for the post comments. Default is MOST_RECENT.

parameters.name: comment_id
parameters.description:
The id of the comment to get replies from.
`Linkedin`: use the comment `id` returned by the comments list.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: The id of the account to perform the request from.

parameters.name: post_id

`Instagram`: Need to use the **provider_id**. Short code cannot be used here (***www.instagram.com/p/SHORTCODE***)

info.title: Unipile
info.description: Unipile Communication is an **HTTP API**. It has predictable resource-oriented `URLs`, accepts **form-encoded** or **JSON-encoded** request bodies, returns **JSON-encoded responses**, and uses standard HTTP response codes, authentication, and verbs.

x-auth-vars.description: Unipile Access Token from the Unipile dashboard; sent as the X-API-KEY header.

CalendarEventCreatedWebhookPayload.title: CalendarEventCreatedWebhookPayload
CalendarEventCreatedWebhookPayload.description: Default JSON payload delivered for calendar_event_created webhooks.

id.description: The ID of the calendar event.

ical_uid.description: The iCalendar UID of the event, as defined in RFC5545.

master_event_id.description: If event instance, the ID of the master event.

calendar_id.description: The ID of the calendar the event belongs to.

created_at.description: The date the event was created. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

updated_at.description: The date the event was last updated. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

is_attendees_list_hidden.description: Is the attendees list hidden for attendees.

items.description: An attendee of a calendar event.

comment.description: The response comment of the attendee.

is_organizer.description: Is the attendee the organizer of the event.

is_optional.description: Is the attendee optional (based on type).

is_resource.description: Is the attendee a resource (based on type).

response_status.description: The response status of the attendee. `yes` if the invitation is accepted. `no` if the invitation is declined. `maybe` if the attendee is not sure. `noreply` if the invitation is pending.

start.description: The start date and time of the event.

date_time.description: The date and time. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

time_zone.description: The time zone of the date time.

date.description: The date. Uses ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD).

end.description: The end date and time of the event.

date_time.description: The date and time. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

time_zone.description: The time zone of the date time.

date.description: The date. Uses ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD).

recurrence.description: List of RRULE, EXRULE, RDATE and EXDATE lines for a recurring event, as specified in RFC5545.

transparency.description: The transparency of the event. `opaque` does block time on the calendar and is equivalent to setting Show me as to Busy in the Calendar UI. `transparent` does not block time on the calendar and is equivalent to setting Show me as to Available in the Calendar UI.

url.description: The conference URL. If not provided, it will automatically create a new conference (only teams and google_meet available)
